14. The appellant and the other accused persons filed an application on January 26, 1991 under section 339C of the Code of Criminal Procedure praying for stoppage of the proceeding against them and for releasing them on the ground that the learned Sessions Judge, Munshiganj, received the record of the case for trial on December 1, 1988 and failed to conclude the trial within the period of 240 days or within the extended period of another 30 days and thereby 270 working days had already expired on November 11, 1989. Their further case was that the case was transferred in the meantime to the Court of Assistant Judge, Munshiganj who again transferred the case to the learned Sessions Judge on January 6, 1990 for want of jurisdiction. The learned Sessions Judge received back the record on January 13, 1990. The appellant and other accused persons then filed the aforesaid application under section 339C of the Code of Criminal Procedure on 26 January 1991; but the learned Sessions Judge dismissed their application by his order dated January 26, 1991 taking the view that since he obtained the charge of the Sessions Division as Sessions Judge with effect from January 23, 1991 fresh limitation will run from January 23, 1991 under sub-section (2) of Section 339C CrPC. On March 5, 1991 the accused-appellant filed another application on the same ground but the learned Sessions Judge refused to take a different view of the matter. Thereafter, the appellant along with 15 other accused persons moved the High Court Division under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure praying for setting aside the orders dated January 26, 1991 and March 5, 1991 passed by the learned Sessions Judge and for quashing the proceeding in Sessions Case No. 26 of 1988 -pending in the Court of Sessions Judge, Munshiganj. A Division Bench of the High Court Division by the impugned judgment and order discharged the Rule observing that in the order dated January 26, 1991 the learned Sessions Judge found that 270 working days was not passed on that date and the appellant could show no ground against the calculation of the learned Sessions Judge. 

 16. With regard to the first point on which leave has been granted, we have no hesitation in holding that the learned Sessions Judge was wrong in holding that since he obtained the charge of the Sessions Division with effect from January 23, 1991, fresh limitation will run from January 23, 1991.
